title: The Bosphorus Brief — Monday, 5 October 2026
overview: A cluster of earthquakes near Adana was the day's main physical event, though no injuries were reported. Otherwise it was a quieter news day, with steady developments on residence permit procedures for students and continuing updates from the northern Cyprus ferry disaster investigation.

sections.heading: Earthquakes near Adana: no injuries, but worth noting
sections.body: Five shallow earthquakes shook southern Turkey on Sunday, with USGS recording magnitudes up to M5.0 near Feke and Saimbeyli in Adana province — close to the epicenter of the deadly 2023 quakes. Tremors were felt as far as northern Syria. Turkish disaster authorities and Syrian officials both confirmed no injuries or structural damage. For residents in the Adana/Feke area, this is a reminder to keep emergency kits ready, but there is no indication of elevated risk beyond normal seismic activity in the region.

sections.heading: Residence permits: processing comes to campus
sections.body: Eskişehir's Provincial Migration Authority Directorate visited Anadolu University to handle residence permit procedures for international students directly on campus, including fingerprinting, without requiring a trip to the migration office. This follows a broader pattern of migration authorities streamlining paperwork for students at partner universities — a practical convenience worth checking for those enrolled elsewhere, as similar arrangements may exist at other institutions.

sections.heading: Northern Cyprus ferry disaster: toll climbs to 19
sections.body: The death toll from the late-August ferry disaster off northern Cyprus has risen to 19 after another body was recovered over the weekend; nine people remain missing. The update came from the office of TRNC prime minister Ünal Üstel. Both opposition-leaning and pro-government outlets reported the same toll without divergence in framing, suggesting the facts here are not in dispute — the story remains one of ongoing recovery efforts rather than new developments in cause or accountability.

sections.heading: One case flagged in our rights watch
sections.body: A Kurdish journalist described alleged mistreatment during a Turkish detention to a Jerusalem Post reporter — the kind of individual account we flag under standing priorities on legal security for residents, without drawing conclusions beyond what was reported. We'll continue watching for any official response or follow-up.

closing: Stay safe out there, and if you're near Adana, a little extra care this week costs nothing.
